references.text: Here we find the Nazirite vow describing the rules for one consecrated to God, including the prohibition against cutting hair, which directly relates to the command that no razor shall come upon Samson's head.
Rebekah also receives a divine announcement about her coming child, in a similar way that Samson's mother is told she will become pregnant.
Hannah vows that her son Samuel shall be a Nazirite from birth, and that no razor shall come upon his head—a direct parallel vow to the one given concerning Samson.
The Lord's servant is called from the womb, reflecting Samson's calling as a Nazirite from the womb.
Jeremiah was known and chosen by God before he was formed in the womb, reflecting the theme of divine election before birth.
The angel's message to Zechariah about John's birth contains similar elements: an announcement of pregnancy, and that the child will be filled with the Holy Spirit from the womb.
Jesus is called a Nazarene, which some interpret as a connection to the Nazirite vow, although it primarily refers to the town of Nazareth.
The angel Gabriel announces to Mary that she will become pregnant and give birth to a son, in the same way the angel announces Samson's birth.
